summary: This GitHub Docs page explains how to use the concurrency keyword in GitHub Actions to limit how many workflow runs or jobs execute at the same time within a context. By default, jobs and runs execute concurrently, but concurrency groups let at most one running and one pending job or workflow share a group, with optional cancellation of in-progress runs. The page gives YAML examples for job-level and workflow-level groups, fallback values, per-workflow scoping, and branch-specific cancellation.
one_line: GitHub Docs guide to the concurrency keyword in GitHub Actions for limiting jobs and workflow runs to one at a time per group.
key_facts: By default, GitHub Actions allows multiple jobs within the same workflow, multiple workflow runs within the same repository, and multiple workflow runs across a repository owner's account to run concurrently.
The jobs.<job_id>.concurrency keyword ensures that only a single job or workflow using the same concurrency group will run at a time.
A concurrency group can be any string or expression.
Allowed expression contexts for concurrency groups are github, inputs, vars, needs, strategy, and matrix.
When a concurrent job or workflow is queued and another job or workflow in the same group is in progress, the queued one is pending.
There can be at most one running and one pending job in a concurrency group at any time.
Setting cancel-in-progress: true also cancels any currently running job or workflow in the same concurrency group.
Concurrency group names are case insensitive, so 'prod' and 'Prod' are treated as the same group.
Ordering is not guaranteed for jobs or workflow runs using concurrency groups; they are handled in an arbitrary order.
The group expression github.head_ref is only defined on pull_request events, so a fallback such as github.head_ref || github.run_id is needed to avoid a syntax error.
To cancel only in-progress runs of the same workflow, the group can be built with github.workflow, for example ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}.
Cancellation can be made conditional, for example cancel-in-progress: ${{ !contains(github.ref, 'release/')}} so pushes to release branches do not cancel runs.
To check constraints with concurrency or queuing, users can monitor how many jobs are being processed on GitHub-hosted runners in their organization or enterprise.
